mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Anuj, aged 28, and Jas, aged 27, are looking to buy their first home together. Anuj is employed as a solicitor with a gross basic salary of £75,000 and Jas is employed as an accountant with a gross basic salary of £68,000. Each of them have saved in cash ISAs for the last few years and each have a balance of £15,000. Neither of them have invested in their ISAs in the current tax year. Anuj inherited a house from his mother on her death in May 2010. Anuj lived in the house until May 2012 and has let the house to his friend since that time for £750 per month. There is no mortgage outstanding. Anuj’s friend is purchasing the property from Anuj for the current value and has already received a mortgage offer to proceed with this. Anuj currently rents a flat near to his workplace for £800 per month. Jas is a first-time buyer and lives at home with her parents. Anuj and Jas have looked at three properties in South East England and are considering the various assisted purchase schemes on offer. The first property they have found is a new build home at £300,000. The developer offers a National House-Building Council (NHBC) Buildmark guarantee for the property. The second property is a fiveyear-old apartment on sale at £325,000. The final property is also a new build house and this property has a shared ownership scheme available. The full sale price for this home is £450,000 and they may purchase as little as 50% of this amount if they wish to use the shared ownership scheme. Anuj and Jas are now considering which property to purchase and how they can take advantage of the different schemes available. 2024/2025 73 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 If Anuj and Jas wish to take advantage of a Lifetime ISA, they should be aware that
opts: they can each contribute £20,000 to a cash ISA plus an additional £4,000 to a Lifetime ISA in the same tax year.
there will be a 25% bonus applied to the Lifetime ISA, up to a maximum of £1,000 per year.
the Lifetime ISA savings and bonus may be used as a deposit for a new home up to a maximum purchase price of £250,000.
the Lifetime ISA can continue to receive contributions up to age 40 only.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Anuj and Jas proceed with the purchase of the first property, for what period will all property defects be covered under the guarantee provided by the developer?
opts: 1 year.
2 years.
3 years.
10 years.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 74 If Anuj and Jas purchase 50% of the third property using the shared ownership arrangement, in respect their Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) liability they should be aware that
opts: if they make a market value election they will pay £10,000 in total.
if they pay the SDLT in stages they will pay nothing at outset and nothing more until they purchase at least 75% of the full value.
if they pay the SDLT in stages they will pay nothing at outset and nothing more until they purchase all of the property.
if they make a market value election and sell the property before buying a further share they will receive a pro rata refund. 2024/2025 Twelve Short-Form Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Anuj were to remortgage the home that he inherited as a residential mortgage, he should be aware that
opts: he is unlikely to be able to raise a remortgage as the property is tenanted.
he may claim the cost of the mortgage interest against the rental income received for taxation purposes and claim tax relief at his highest marginal rate.
the lender would need to carry out a full affordability assessment for the mortgage.
this would always be treated as a nonregulated mortgage as it is rented to a non-family member.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Anuj and Jas have now discovered that the apartment they are considering is commonhold. They should be aware that
opts: the maximum mortgage term will be the remaining term of the lease less 25 years.
they will have a maximum of a 99-year lease.
they will only have a lifetime interest in the apartment.
they will own the apartment in perpetuity
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Terry and Maria, both aged 50, have lived in their marital home for 10 years and owe £150,000 on their mortgage. The house is currently valued at £475,000. They have recently separated after 15 years of marriage and are trying to reach a financial settlement as part of their divorce. Terry is self-employed and had taxable net profits in the last tax year of £14,629. Maria is employed and has a gross basic salary of £60,000 per annum. Neither of them have any debts outstanding, other than the mortgage. They also own a holiday home as joint tenants, which is unencumbered. This was purchased in May 2012 for £140,000, and is now valued at £278,000. The holiday home has been rented commercially during that time. Maria moved into this property when they separated and there have been no lettings since then. She has NOT declared this house to be her primary residence. Since Maria moved out of the marital home around six months ago, Terry has found it difficult to manage his finances, despite the fact that Maria has made regular payments into their joint bank account to fund the mortgage. Terry has let arrears build up on the mortgage account totalling around £2,200. Recently Terry asked his friend, John, to move in with him to help with the monthly costs. John pays a monthly rent of £400 to Terry and Terry attributes £100 per month of this as costs. Maria is considering purchasing the marital home from Terry as part of the divorce settlement. If she does so, she may let the property to tenants. She is aware that the rental income would be £1,200 per month. Terry and Maria are considering all of their options as part of the divorce settlement. 76 2024/2025 Twelve Short-Form Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Short-Form Case Studies 1 If Maria was to acquire Terry’s share of the marital home as part of the divorce settlement and agrees to take on the mortgage, how much Stamp Duty Land Tax would she pay, if any?
opts: Nil.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If Maria were to receive the holiday home as part of the divorce settlement and decided to continue to live in the property, in respect of private residence relief she should be aware that
opts: before she can claim private residence relief, she will need to pay Capital Gains Tax on the increase in value up to the date of the divorce.
if she has claimed furnished holiday letting relief in the past, then this property cannot be categorised as her primary residence.
she may elect for this to be her primary residence and has up to two years to make the election from the date she occupied the property.
she may not elect for this property to be her primary residence unless Terry makes a joint nomination as part of the divorce settlement.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 3 Maria and Terry have elected to sell the holiday home for £278,000. If they sold the property in May 2023, and assuming that Maria had already used her Capital Gains Tax (CGT) exemption in that tax year, how much CGT would Maria pay on her share of the sale proceeds?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 78 In respect of the rental income Terry receives from John, Terry should be aware that
opts: as this property is jointly owned, he may not claim rent-a-room relief.
if he elects not to use rent-a-room relief, he will pay Income Tax of £720 on the rent he receives from John.
if Terry charges John for any meals he makes he may not claim rent-a-room relief on the money received.
using rent-a-room relief, he may also rent another room to another tenant for an amount of £3,900 per annum without paying Income Tax on the proceeds. 2024/2025 Twelve Short-Form Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: In respect of the mortgage arrears, Terry and Maria should be aware that
opts: if Maria proceeds to purchase the house outright, the current lender will always require that she and Terry remain as joint mortgagors.
the lender may only consider repossession after applying for a suspended possession order.
they may only offer peaceable possession once arrears amount to three monthly payments.
they will both remain responsible for the balance outstanding, irrespective of who is living at the property.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Darren and Julia are first-time buyers who have come to the Glenrothes Building Society for a loan. They have asked for an explanation of the various mortgage and protection products available and for assistance in helping them decide which are appropriate for their circumstances. Darren is 27 and has been self-employed since qualifying as an electrician. He was made bankrupt at 23 when a large client went out of business before paying him. He was discharged after two years. Since then, he has built a new business and now makes a gross profit of £30,000 pa. Julia is 25 and has been a self-employed hairdresser since she was 21, earning £19,000 pa. This is her only income. Now that Darren has rebuilt his business, Julia’s parents have doubled her savings of £15,000 to enable them to put a deposit on a flat, for which they have offered £145,000 against the asking price of £149,995. Darren’s parents are assisting with other moving expenses and some basic furniture. Though their budget is limited, they are anxious to ensure that Darren and Julia make appropriate checks regarding the property. Their proposed flat is in a block of 6 in the town centre. The block was constructed in 1960 and has recently had repairs to the roof and windows. Darren wishes to reduce their outstanding capital as soon as possible. Julia feels that life cover may be important for starting a family. Both agree that stability of expenses and cost savings in the early years is essential. However, they do not want to suffer any subsequent penalties unless they are in a position to repay their loan. 2024/2025 83 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 With regard to Darren’s declared status:
opts: He cannot borrow by law.
He is only allowed by law to borrow nominal amounts.
the Society cannot legally refuse to lend.
the Society can consider the application on its merits.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The Society will require Julia to provide financial information including all of the following, EXCEPT:
opts: three years profit and loss accounts.
regular sales commissions and bonuses.
a business plan.
annual turnover.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: With regard to Darren, the Society is likely to:
opts: disregard business data before age 25.
only consider fully audited accounts.
pay particular attention to trends in business performance.
rely mainly on business projections if signed by his accountant.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 84 Concerning the flat Darren and Julia wish to purchase, the Society will mainly require the following additional information.
opts: The exact tenure of the property.
Its proximity to a railway station.
The state of décor of the other flats.
If there is a management committee. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The MOST appropriate survey and valuation product to satisfy the criteria of Darren’s parents would:
opts: rely solely on that commissioned by the Society.
reveal certain defects but provide little guarantee.
ensure significant defects are revealed but without comeback.
both reveal major defects and provide some comeback.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The mortgage repayment method which would satisfy Darren’s stated criteria is designed to:
opts: repay increasing proportions of interest over the term.
provide a potential tax-free cash surplus at the end of the term.
ensure repayment on premature death or long-term disability.
enable subsequent further borrowing without the need of top-up investment.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 MCOB rules state that early repayment charges applied to their mortgage must be capable of being expressed as a cash value and be:
opts: a reasonable estimate of the costs of ending the contract early.
calculated to a maximum of three months interest.
no more than a certain percentage of the initial mortgage advance, as specified by the regulator.
only applicable to fixed-rate and cappedrate mortgages.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 8 Darren and Julia’s requirements in the early years indicate a mortgage product which will:
opts: generate an immediate cash lump sum.
enable them to set the rate of interest payable.
allow regular underpayments compensated by overpayments.
enable accurate budgeting without increasing outstanding capital.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The mortgage repayment method favoured by Darren is:
opts: usually combined with a decreasing amount of cover.
most commonly protected by a static amount of cover.
automatically includes critical illness.
allows protection to be upgraded without further medical evidence.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 86 What is the position with Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on their proposed purchase?
opts: They will be exempt from SDLT.
They will pay SDLT on the purchase price and the annual ground rent combined.
They will pay SDLT on the full purchase price.
They will pay SDLT on the price offered and accepted. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Linda and Carl have offered £169,950 for their first house. Linda, aged 24, is employed as a manager of a fashion store. Carl, aged 26, is employed as marketing manager for an engineering company. Linda’s employer provides full sick pay for six months, and life cover of twice her salary of £28,000. No occupational pension scheme or other benefits are currently provided. Linda has made no private provision. Carl’s employer provides full sick pay for six months and half pay for a further six months. He is a member of the company’s defined benefit occupational pension scheme, with a retirement age of 65. He has no other private provision. He currently earns £35,000 p.a. In addition to this basic salary, he has received profit sharing bonuses of £3,000, £3,500 and £3,750 for the last three years. They wish to borrow £154,500 and are aware that the lender would require a Higher Lending Charge in excess of 80% LTV. They are anxious to ensure they are fully protected, subject to affordability. As the house is newly built and guaranteed, they wish to avoid unnecessary expense in this area. They would like a mortgage product that would allow them to make capital reductions and, perhaps, be adaptable to fit in with their regular holidays. Neither is a keen investor, preferring to either spend on holidays, or reduce their debt to release further borrowing capacity. They have been informed that their application will result in a credit check and want to know what rights they have regarding the information obtained. 88 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 When assessing their borrowing capacity, the lender is likely to consider Carl’s profit sharing bonuses as:
opts: guaranteed regular income.
additional income only after five years.
an averaged additional income.
completely irrelevant.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: With regard to the information obtained by the lender under the credit check, Linda and Carl can:
opts: only obtain details with the lender’s permission.
only have access to that held on computer by the lender.
have access only to computerised records but on payment of a fee.
have access to any paper or computer based details held.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The MOST appropriate survey and valuation product under Linda and Carl’s stated circumstances would:
opts: be that commissioned solely by the lender.
be likely to reveal most defects, but without guarantees.
ensure all major defects are revealed, but without guarantees.
ensure all major defects are revealed and provide guarantees.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 The survey and valuation product identified in question 3 will cover all of the following, EXCEPT:
opts: a sketch of the property.
details of landslip in the surrounding area.
recommended conditions applicable to the advance.
underlying defects in the foundations.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5
opts: s a result of the valuation, the lender is LEAST likely to recommend in respect of Linda and Darren’s property: A retention.
undertaking.
acceptance.
minor repairs.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The MOST appropriate mortgage repayment method to meet Linda and Darren’s objectives:
opts: attracts tax relief on the monthly payments.
has automatic built-in life cover.
automatically reduces the interest payable.
provides a potential tax free surplus.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The mortgage product that fits Linda and Carl’s stated criteria could offer any of the following, EXCEPT:
opts: a genuinely lower interest rate for the initial period.
a lump sum in excess of the mortgage amount.
the facility to miss payments on a regular basis.
an equity-linked savings plan to fund regular overpayments.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 90 The product which would provide the MOST comprehensive coverage for long-term sickness, for the main earner, should:
opts: also include cover for unemployment.
have a 52 week deferred period.
have a sum insured of at least £154,500.
be specifically linked to the monthly loan payments. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If affordability of the product identified in question 8 proves to be an issue, Linda and Carl should consider:
opts: shortening the deferred period.
excluding unemployment cover.
alternative cover for a shorter payment period.
an alternative product covering a specified list of illnesses.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The sum insured required under the HLC, based on their offer price, would be:
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Andy and Sue are buying their first property in the UK. They have been living and working in Germany for the past 5 years, where they rented an apartment. Andy is 28 and a structural engineer. He feels he has excellent prospects with his new employer, including the opportunity to work in Eastern Europe. His current salary is £50,000 p.a. Sue is 27 and expecting their first child in 3 months’ time. They have agreed that she will not look for a new job for at least one year. They have seen a Victorian house that they love, and have offered £290,000 against the asking price of £295,950. They have saved £29,000 for a deposit, plus enough to cover initial moving expenses. They understand that the lender, that has been recommended by their adviser, requires a higher lending charge (HLbut do not understand the implications of this. They are also anxious to ensure the property represents a sound investment. Andy’s father has offered to act as guarantor should this be required. Andy would like to know what obligations this imposes on his father. They are unsure what mortgage products would be appropriate for their circumstances, but wish to maximise their future borrowing capacity. They have friends who have foreign currency loans, and they would like more information on these. They also wonder if, whilst Sue is not working, a low start arrangement may be more appropriate and would like details of any suitable schemes. Their adviser will receive a proc fee of £220. Lenders also offers various property insurance options. Andy and Sue are particularly interested in the index linking option and wonder whether it is possible for this to result in over-insurance. 92 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 In the circumstances indicated, the lender is likely to be MOST interested in which one of the following details on the mortgage application form?
opts: Sue’s most recent annual salary.
Andy’s former UK employment history.
Their property rental history.
Their lack of current dependants.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: With regard to available survey and valuation products, their stated objective indicates that:
opts: the report commissioned by the lender will be adequate.
they should ensure they have some comeback in the future.
a middle of the road approach provides sufficient guarantees.
whilst all options should reveal defects, cost is the main consideration.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 The mortgage repayment method which matches their stated objective will:
opts: include a gradually reducing interest element.
be supported by a low risk investment product.
require a specified rate of capital growth.
offer a potential tax-free lump sum at maturity.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 4 When assessing the affordability of their application:
opts: Andy and Sue must undergo a full affordability assessment.
Andy could choose to self-certify his income.
Andy could elect to be treated as a business customer.
The lender could offer Andy and Sue an execution-only process.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: To comply with the MCOB rules on initial disclosure, what must Andrew's adviser inform him about the lender’s procuration fee?
opts: There is no requirement to mention the fee, as Andrew will not be paying it.
The adviser must inform Andrew of the exact amount of the fee.
The adviser must only state that the fee is around £250.
The adviser need only indicate that a payment is to be received.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 94 If they opt for a Tracker Mortgage, the interest rate they will pay will be influenced by decisions made by:
opts: the Bank of England Financial Policy Committee.
the Bank of England Monetary Policy
ommittee. C the Financial Conduct Authority.
UK Finance. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: With regard to their interest in foreign currency mortgages, they should be aware that:
opts: these are only appropriate when sterling is in decline.
such a mortgage is only possible while Andy is paid in sterling.
new loans must be based on the Euro.
consideration should wait until Andy’s income basis changes.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If a claim is made under the HLC policy,
opts: ndy and Sue: A will have their mortgage payments met for a fixed period.
will have no further obligation with regard to the mortgage.
could be forced to repay the amount paid out under the policy.
may be legally obliged to pay additional compensation to the lender.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

opts: ndy’s father should be made aware that he is: A entitled to be released from his obligations on request.
only relieved of his responsibilities with the lender’s permission.
responsible for ensuring Andy and Sue make payments when due.
only required to make a payment when the HLC leaves a shortfall.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 10 With regard to the index-linking facility under property insurance policies, Andy and Sue should be made aware that:
opts: this is now compulsory for both buildings and contents.
increases will be matched to the market value of the property.
reductions may be negotiated subject to an indemnity clause.
reductions are only granted when property prices have fallen.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Clare started her 25-year variable-rate interest-only mortgage ten years ago using a unit-linked endowment policy as the repayment vehicle, which is assigned to the lender. The current rate of interest currently charged is 6.4%. The loan amount was more than covered by her salary at the time, of £37,000. Since her redundancy two months ago she has been unable to find work. Clare is now two months in arrears and has no insurance policy on which to claim, although she submitted a claim for Support Mortgage Interest (SMI) as soon as she went into arrears. The ten-year review of her endowment policy shows a projected maturity value of £65,000, against the loan amount of £75,000. The insurance company has recommended an increase to her monthly premiums of £90, but Clare doesn’t want to do this and is looking for an alternative solution. Her boyfriend Nick has returned from Voluntary Service Overseas and will be moving in with her. They are planning to get married when their joint financial situation improves. In the meantime Nick will help pay the household bills and is anxious to help Clare to clear the mortgage arrears. Clare would like Nick to be added to the mortgage deed and he has agreed to this. The couple have also discussed renting their spare room to a lodger which the lender has provisionally indicated it may permit. Nick is starting a new job as a warehouse manager on an annual salary of £35,000. His employer offers no benefits package. Clare and Nick have arranged an appointment with Gerry, an adviser at their lender, to discuss their situation. Clare has had her house valued by a local estate agent who has stated that if sold, the property should be put on the market for £150,000. 2024/2025 97 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 Which potential solution to Clare’s arrears situation would be the most appropriate?
opts: Surrender the endowment policy
Suspend monthly mortgage payments
Clear the debt over a set period.
Extend the mortgage term.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What is Clare’s situation regarding receipt of Support for Mortgage Interest (SMI)?
opts: 50% of her interest will have been paid from month 2
50% of her interest will become payable after a further 15 weeks.
No interest will be payable for approximately another 31 weeks.
No interest will be payable for approximately another 5 weeks
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which of the following would be covered under Clare’s claim for Support for Mortgage Interest?
opts: Mortgage interest
Mortgage interest plus endowment premiums
Mortgage interest plus endowment premiums plus arrears
Mortgage interest plus endowment premiums plus arrears plus buildings insurance premiums
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 98 What is likely to be required from their lender if Claire goes ahead with her intention to occupy the spare room with a lodger?
opts: A formal rental agreement between her and the lodger.
A signed consent to mortgage form.
Proof of income from the lodger.
Formal submission to HMRC for the rental paid to Claire 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Before Nick is added to the mortgage deed, he should be made aware that he:
opts: must sign a consent to mortgage form.
will be subject to the normal status enquiries before the legal procedure is carried out.
loses his rights under the Family Law Act 1996
must also be added to the endowment policy.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: With regard to the couple’s proposals for the spare room, Gerry, their adviser, should point out that
opts: any occupant should undergo standard status enquiries.
the lender will want to ensure that no right of residence is created.
this will extend Clare’s waiting period for Support for Mortgage Interest.
the lender will collect rent to offset the arrears under their right as Mortgagee in Possession.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If Clare, with the lender’s agreement, surrenders her endowment policy and switches to capital repayment, what is the key disadvantage for her?
opts: An income tax liability could arise.
The surrender value she receives may be spent unwisely.
A large redemption penalty could be imposed by the lender.
Her mortgage payments would increase and alternative life cover may need to be arranged.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 8 If Clare chose to keep the endowment policy, how could a potential shortfall risk be minimised?
opts: Extending the mortgage term.
Linking part of the loan to Equity ISAs.
Converting part of the loan to a repayment basis.
Converting the endowment policy to a unitised with-profits basis.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The results of the valuation will indicate to their lender that at this stage :
opts: a further advance is viable.
the Society’s interests remain protected.
Clare and Nick should consider trading down.
Clare and Nick need not follow the insurer’s recommendation.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 100 Once their lender became aware that the account was in arrears, it was required to write to them within:
opts: 5 business days.
7 business days.
15 business days.
30 business days. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Five years ago Gary and Amy took out a £125,000 joint interest-only mortgage with the Hoddesdon Building Society. At that time Gary was earning £34,000, Amy was earning £16,000 and no higher lending charge was required. The original draft of their mortgage deed submitted to Gary and Amy’s solicitor had a further advance clause in it, but due to a last minute change in lending policy it was removed in the final signed version. Six months ago due to a failed marriage, Gary’s brother Alan moved in and pays £120 per week rent. Last month Gary took out a 4 year personal loan to buy a second hand car. They now plan to build an extension and are in the process of applying for a further advance of £30,000 from their existing lender. Last month Amy finally decided to give up work for several years, due to the imminent arrival of their first child. They intend Alan to remain as a lodger after the baby is born. When they first started the mortgage, the house was worth £200,000. 102 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 Which of the following is least likely to be required in relation to the new mortgage arrangement?
opts: A credit search on both applicants.
A higher lending charge.
Evidence of income for both applicants.
Expenditure details for both applicants.

mcqs.q: Assuming Gary does not intend to repay his personal loan from the further advance proceeds, when assessing affordability, the lender would regard the personal loan repayments as:
opts: basic essential expenditure.
basic discretionary expenditure.
committed expenditure.
quality-of-living expenditure.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Tacking of the further advance:
opts: is not appropriate in this case.
will reduce the priority of the initial mortgage.
will reduce the priority of the further advance.
requires the execution of a deed of variation.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If Gary and Amy’s lender insists on a higher lending charge where the further advance exceeds the loan-to-value ratio threshold of 75%, this further advance will:
opts: not require a high loan policy.
exceed the threshold by £4,000.
exceed the threshold by £5,000.
represent an overall loan-to-value ratio of 80%.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5 The decision taken by Amy last month:
opts: will ensure that the additional loan is treated as unregulated.
will ensure that income corroboration is not required.
could affect whether or not the lender requires a property valuation.
could affect whether or not the lender agrees to the additional loan.

seek independent legal advice.
submit details of his income.
provide a surety or guarantee.

mcqs.q: When processing the new loan application, a statutory obligation is placed on Gary and

abide by the terms of MCOB.
check the adequacy of the security.
obtain written corroboration of income.

opts: Nothing.
£500. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If the further advance fails to be granted, this could result in:
opts: an entry being placed in the credit agency register
Alan acquiring an overriding interest in the property under the Land Registration Act.
the original loan being reclassified as exempt order under the Consumer Credit Act.
a deed of variation being issued to Gary and Amy.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If the original version of the mortgage deed had been used, what effect could this have had on the further advance?

Additional stamp duty would become payable.
Additional land registry fees would become payable.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Lynn and Jason, both aged 24, have been savers with the East Hertfordshire Building Society for three years, and now have £7,500 in their joint savings account towards a deposit and moving expenses for their first property. They expect to use £6,000 for the deposit, and whilst keeping other expenses low wish to ensure that they are making a sensible purchase. They would like a mortgage with the Society and are interested in a product that would effectively reduce their costs in the early years, so they can furnish their property. They have offered £59,995 for a small leasehold flat, for which the advertised price was £61,000, and you have explained that the lender will require a higher lending fee for loans to value exceeding 80%. The flat is in the town centre above a chemist and has an unexpired lease of 40 years. There is a further flat above theirs. They want to know how the main mortgage repayment methods, and protection products work, as they are unsure which they would prefer. Both Lynn and Jason are self-employed in their joint 2year-old interior design business, drawing £14,000 each. They are concentrating on building their business for the next few years, in the expectation of purchasing a larger property before starting a family. 2024/2025 107 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 In order to assess their ability to pay, Lynn and Jason’s circumstances particularly require them to provide:
opts: audited profit and loss accounts from outset.
projections prepared by a qualified accountant.
a business plan formally approved by their bank manager.
bank statements for the three years prior to the start of their business.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If their offer is accepted, how much stamp duty, if any, will they save compared to purchasing at the asking price?
opts: None.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 108 With regard to the value of Lynn and Jason’s proposed property, the Society is LEAST likely to be concerned about:
opts: whether Lynn and Jason can run their business from home.
rights of way through and around the chemist shop.
maintenance provisions for the communal areas.
Lynn and Jason’s rights regarding purchase of the freehold. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: To meet their stated objectives, the MOST appropriate survey and valuation product will:
opts: be commissioned by the Society.
be expected to reveal any major defects.
give Lynn and Jason full comeback if defects are undiscovered.
provide a warranty that the purchase price is reasonable.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The interest only mortgage repayment vehicle, which is specifically designed to meet Lynn and Jason’s expenditure objectives in the early years will:
opts: increase in cost after a specified period.
increase the outstanding capital after an initial period.
ensure a tax-free lump sum surplus at the end of the term.
provide tax-free growth with easy regular access to capital.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 The advantage of the repayment vehicle, specifically designed to meet Lynn and Jason’s expenditure objectives, over a capital repayment mortgage, is:
opts: the facility to repay early without penalty.
built-in protection against premature death.
guaranteed repayment by the end of the term.
flexibility to cope with changing circumstances.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 7 The mortgage product which will effectively meet Lynn and Jason’s early years’ costs objective, despite requiring payments at the standard variable rate, will:
opts: cause an increase in the capital outstanding after the initial period.
limit the maximum monthly payment for a specified period.
offer a genuine discount without penalty.
offer a lump sum without increasing the capital.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The possible drawback of the product identified in question 7, with regard to Lynn and Jason’s stated objectives, is the:
opts: potential penalty on moving house.
substantial up-front arrangement fee.
necessity for a minimum 20% deposit.
higher subsequent interest payments.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The product MOST commonly used to protect the alternative mortgage repayment to that used in question 5, would provide:
opts: level cover over the mortgage term.
gradually reducing cover for a level premium.
the option to upgrade cover without medical evidence.
include an investment element which could provide a surplus.

mcqs.q: 110 In order to avoid the Higher Lending Charge, Lynn and Jason would need to deposit a further:
opts: £7,000. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Benjamin Sarah and Benjamin are first time buyers. They have offered £149,950 for a leasehold flat, and have saved a deposit of £22,500, plus their other house purchase expenses. Benjamin, aged 23, currently rents a bedsit. He earns £27,000 p.a. as a trainee solicitor. He hopes to qualify in two years, following which his earnings should increase significantly. Sarah, aged 22, has not worked for the last year due to a long-term viral illness. She is a qualified beautician, and hopes to start work again soon on a part-time, selfemployed basis. They have no children, but hope to start a family when Benjamin has qualified and Sarah has recovered from her illness. Benjamin’s employer does not provide an occupational pension scheme, but offers full pay on sickness for the first three months and half pay for a further three months. They are concerned as to how their mortgage would be repaid if Benjamin were ill for longer than this. Sarah and Benjamin have explained to their mortgage broker that they have a very cautious attitude to risk and would like to keep costs low, at least until Benjamin qualifies. They have little understanding of the procedures of the products available, but have heard of unit-linked endowments. They have asked for a full explanation of everything involved. The preferred lender for Sarah and Benjamin requires a Higher Lending Charge for cases in excess of 75% loan to value. 112 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 Sarah and Benjamin will be expected to provide various details in order to corroborate their income. All of the following would be relevant, EXCEPT:
opts: 6 months’ joint bank account statements.
Sarah’s most recent P60.
Benjamin’s employer’s reference.
Benjamin’s landlord’s reference.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The level of valuation report on which the lender will insist will reveal:
opts: the building and contents insurance required.
if Sarah and Benjamin need a Home Buyer’s Report.
the full repairs Sarah and Benjamin should make.
if Sarah and Benjamin are paying too much.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If the lender’s normal valuation report indicates acceptance, this will confirm to Sarah and Benjamin that the:
opts: flat has no defects.
flat’s decorative state is excellent.
amount requested is in line with the market value.
market value matches the insurance value.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 4 It will be explained that the advantage of a unit-linked endowment mortgage, in Sarah and Benjamin’s circumstances, would be:
opts: potential for high growth from a choice of low risk funds.
avoidance of additional costs to provide life cover.
availability of high levels of joint cover regardless of health.
facility to include protection against long term illness.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Sarah and Benjamin’s profile and circumstances indicate that a unit-linked endowment mortgage may be inappropriate as:
opts: Sarah would automatically be declined.
they are waiting before starting a family.
available funds all carry an element of risk.
Benjamin’s employer already provides suitable benefits.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 114 Taking into account the information Sarah and Benjamin have provided, the MOST suitable method of mortgage repayment for them would:
opts: gradually reduce the amount of interest being paid.
provide the potential for a tax-free lump sum surplus.
allow potential early repayment if fund growth exceeds expectations.
include an element of life cover to protect against early death. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Sarah and Benjamin’s circumstances indicate that the appropriate mortgage product would:
opts: be linked closely to the Bank of England base rate.
allow regular underpayments in the early years.
ensure reduced repayments for a fixed period with subsequent increased capital.
allow initial payments below the standard rate without penalty.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Sarah and Benjamin’s stated circumstances indicate that the MOST appropriate product to protect against sickness in the early years of their mortgage would:
opts: meet their mortgage expenses for a maximum of two years.
continue to provide an income until Benjamin retires.
pay a lump sum if either contracted a specified illness.
also cover either of them in periods of unemployment.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If the product identified in question 8 is taken up and protection is extended when Benjamin qualifies, the MOST comprehensive additional policy should be arranged to provide:
opts: an income for Benjamin after six months’ illness.
an income for Benjamin after two years’ illness.
an immediate lump sum should either become seriously ill.
payment of their mortgage and related expenses should either become unemployed.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 10 Which of the following actions is the adviser obliged to take in order to comply with the MCOB rules in dealing with Sarah and Benjamin’s
opts: Explain the lender's process for assessing their ability to repay the loan.
Give them the reasons for recommending the mortgage immediately after their application has been received.
Give them a full list of mortgage lenders who offer a similar contract.
Inform them of any limitations on the range of products the firm can offer.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Norris is hoping to purchase his first property in the South West of England for £200,000 with the help of a mortgage from the Wessex Bank. Three of Norris’s four children will also occupy the property: Amy, aged 17; Simon, aged 16; and Sharon, aged 14. Norris was widowed last year at the age of 40. He is employed as a training manager, having resigned as a sales executive when his wife died. However, as his net monthly salary has now reduced significantly to £1,950, he is keen to keep his monthly payments as low as possible for the first few years. Norris received the proceeds of her life assurance policy. He plans to use up to £75,000 of this to provide the deposit for his property after settling some debts and helping his eldest daughter Alison with a property deposit. Norris’s intended property underwent structural alteration a few years ago and is now in urgent need of redecoration. He has asked a chartered surveyor friend to carry out a Building Survey and has been promised the report within the next few days. Norris is anxious to ensure that his monthly mortgage payments can continue to be met should he be unable to work due to ill health, at least in the short term, and he wishes to be able to leave the house to his children without debt. His company pays full salary for the first month of absence; he has no other work-related benefits other than membership of the NEST pension scheme. Norris has estimated that his monthly expenditure in the new house before mortgage payments will be committed expenditure: £150; basic essential expenditure: £700; basic quality-of-living expenditure: £200 The Wessex Bank mortgage adviser has recommended a variable-rate repayment mortgage with a 1.5% discount for the first two years. The bank uses a stressed mortgage interest rate of 5% to calculate affordability, which works out at £5.85 per month per 1,000 borrowed. The maximum monthly loan repayments cannot exceed 85% of Norris’s monthly free disposable income. Norris’s daughter, Alison, is hoping to buy a flat with her boyfriend. She has found a flat with a purchase price of £120,000 and Norris has promised to help with the deposit from what remains of his wife’s life assurance payment. 2024/2025 117 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 What might be the consequences of Norris's surveyor friend carrying out the survey?
opts: It will prevent Norris from taking legal action if any defects are omitted.
Norris will be prevented from using the survey report in negotiations with the vendor.
The bank may still require an independent valuation.
The surveyor must complete a special declaration for the bank.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What recommendation is the valuer most likely to make to the bank in respect of the work that Norris feels must be done urgently?
opts: A retention pending satisfactory completion of the work.
A written undertaking from Norris to complete the work within a specified period.
Decline the application because the loanto-value ratio is high.
That a higher interest rate is applied to the mortgage.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 118 Which of the following is true in relation to the mortgage product recommended by Norris’s adviser?
opts: Early repayment charges do not usually apply to this sort of arrangement.
It will provide Norris with security against interest rate rises.
The lender may include a minimum interest rate in the terms and conditions of the mortgage.
There is no product fee charged for this sort of arrangement. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Using Wessex Bank’s affordability criteria, approximately what is the maximum mortgage Norris could arrange?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: One of the main benefits of the product recommended by Wessex Bank is that:
opts: Norris can benefit from any interest rate decreases.
the discount will only be repayable at the end of the term.
the monthly payment cannot rise above a set amount.
the monthly payment is fixed throughout the mortgage term.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Which of the following statements is true in relation to the proposed new remortgage?
opts: The application will be subject to all MCOB requirements on advice, suitability and affordability.
The lender can waive an affordability assessment in view of Norris’s payment record.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 7 The most appropriate life assurance policy for the new mortgage is a type of:
opts: convertible term assurance.
decreasing term assurance.
mortgage payment protection insurance.
level term assurance.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: In Norris's current circumstances, the most appropriate product to meet his mortgage repayments, should he fall ill, would provide what form of payment? A:
opts: lump sum payable directly to his lender.
lump sum payable to him to use as he requires.
monthly payment for up to two years.
monthly payment that continues until he retires.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which of the following would apply to sale of any protection products Norris was advised to take out by the bank’s adviser?
opts: A 28-day cancellation period.
MCOB rules.
The adviser must give Norris a statement of demand and needs.
The adviser must give Norris a suitability report.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 120 Which of the following would be included in Norris’s committed expenditure figure?
opts: Childcare Costs.
Council Tax Payments.
Electricity Costs.
Opted-in Pension Contribution. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Michael started a £60,000 endowment mortgage in 2003 when he was manager of the electrical department of a high street store. The mortgage lender is the Royal Linslade Bank. The endowment provider is Scottish & General Assurance plc; the policy was assigned to the lender. Two years’ ago, due to poor trading conditions, the entire department was closed down and he was made redundant. Since then he has been unsuccessful in finding a new job and has run into difficulties meeting his monthly payments. Consequently he has built up mortgage interest arrears of £2,200 which the Bank are considering disclosing to Credit Tank plc, a national credit reference agency. He has recently been discussing the matter with Angela, a financial counsellor with Stepchange. As a result of his financial difficulties, Michael has successfully applied for Support for Mortgage Interest (SMI). Three months into the claim period he had an interview for a new job. Two months ago his Aunt Maude died and last week he heard through family sources that he might be in line for a five figure bequest. His current mortgage interest rate is 5.25% - Base Rate Tracker - and the ‘standard rate’ for SMI purposes is currently 5.75%. His monthly payments to Scottish & General are £85.50 and he also currently pays £30 per month Insurance-By-Phone plc for buildings insurance cover. 122 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 What initial advice should Angela offer to Michael regarding his current circumstances?
opts: Approach Royal Linslade Bank to make an arrangement.
Ensure that any new partner signs a consent to mortgage form immediately.
Obtain the relevant Citizens Advice information pack.
Seek a new lender who will consolidate any arrears.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: How much Support Mortgage Interest does Michael receive, if any, in week 6 of his claim?
opts: Nothing.
25% of the interest.
50% of the interest.
100% of the interest.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: In the week of his job interview, what level of SMI, if any, will be payable in respect of Michael’s claim?
opts: Nothing.
25% of the interest.
50% of the interest.
The full amount of interest.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Income Support payments made under Michael’s claim are currently paid:
opts: directly to Michael.
directly to the Royal Linslade Bank.
jointly to Scottish & General and the Royal Linslade Bank.
jointly to Michael and the Royal Linslade Bank.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5
opts: t what rate of mortgage interest are Income Support payments under Michael’s claim currently made? A 5.0%.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What proportion of Michael’s monthly payments of £115.50, if any, is covered by SMI interest payments?
opts: None of it.
All of it.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Michael has been informed that his property is subject to chancel repair liability. If this is the case, notice of the liability will have been registered by the:
opts: previous owner.
local authority.
local parish council.
parochial church council.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 124 Under MCOBs, the Bank are only permitted to discuss the mortgage arrears with Angela PROVIDED:
opts: arrears represent more than 6 months’ interest.
they give Michael 28 days’ prior notice.
Michael asks them to.
Angela has signed a declaration of confidentiality. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Michael decides to apply for a secondcharge loan rather than a further advance to his current mortgage, which of the following is true?
opts: There may be a restriction at HM Land Registry requiring the first-charge lender’s agreement for any second charge.
A second-charge holder has equitable rights over the property.
The second-charge loan is likely to be at a lower interest rate than the existing mortgage.
The second-charge loan must end at the same time as the existing mortgage.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which of the following would give Michael’s lender the right to surrender his endowment policy to help clear the arrears?
opts: Assignment of the policy.
Beneficial security.
Equitable deposit.
The policy being held in trust.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Jason Lawrence, a management consultant, bought a flat three years ago with a 25 year capital repayment mortgage from the Buckingham Building Society. Three months ago he accepted an offer from his employer to take up a two year secondment in the company’s New York offices. Meanwhile his friend, Jason, is coming to the end of a 12 month tenancy agreement and, as it is not renewable, is looking for new accommodation. Jason has seen Lawrence’s flat and is very interested in renting it during the period of Lawrence’s secondment. As he is a good friend, Lawrence is quite keen on the idea of Jason moving in during that time and has been discussing the matter with Shona, who runs a professional letting agency. Lawrence’s monthly mortgage payments to the Society are currently £825. 126 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 If Jason pays rent to Lawrence WITHOUT the knowledge of the Buckingham Building Society, what are the implications?
opts: Lawrence will be in breach of his mortgage.
Jason will be bound by the conditions of Lawrence’s mortgage deed.
The Society is automatically prevented from obtaining vacant possession.
Rental income will be automatically taxed at the rate of 34%.

mcqs.q: If the Society agree to Lawrence’s idea, they are likely to require that:

the Society is co-signatory to the tenancy agreement.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If Jason moves into the flat on an ‘authorised’ basis for the entire secondment period, which of the following changes to Lawrence’s mortgage is MOST likely to happen as a consequence?

The mortgage term will be reduced to 20 years.
The mortgage interest rate will decrease by 0.25%.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 4 If the Society sanctions the rental payments, which aspect of Jason’s proposed tenancy is MOST likely to cause a breach of the letting conditions?
opts: The monthly rent is set at £450.
An assured shorthold tenancy agreement is used.
An independent letting agency is engaged to set up the rental agreement.
The monthly rent is paid by cheques.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which factor is most likely to PREVENT the Society from granting the permission Lawrence would be seeking?
opts: Jason is self employed.
Jason has access to an employer subsidised mortgage scheme.
Lawrence’s mortgage account fell into arrears on three occasions.
Lawrence recently suffered a fall in salary.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 128 When setting up the agreement between Jason and Lawrence, using the services of Shona’s Company:
opts: is not permitted for collection of the rent.
would be a breach of the mortgage deed.
would create an overriding interest.
is likely to satisfy one of the Society’s conditions. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: If Jason moves in before Lawrence receives the lender’s permission, but pays rent regularly, then:
opts: no rights of occupation are conferred.
an overriding interest is automatically created.
no breach of the mortgage covenant will have occurred.
the lender should acknowledge the tenancy to protect its interests.

mcqs.q: HMRC is likely to treat monthly payments by Jason to Lawrence as:
opts: taxable income throughout.
tax free income throughout.
tax free for the first 12 months then as taxable income.
taxable income for the first 12 months then as tax free income.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If the Buckingham Building Society acknowledge Jason’s tenancy even though they withheld permission from Lawrence, what are the implications?
opts: It will prevent an overriding interest from being created.
It will prevent a breach of Jason’s mortgage covenant.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 10 If no approach is made to the Society who subsequently discover that Jason is paying rent for the flat, what is the Society BEST advised to do?
opts: Sanction the tenancy within 6 months of Jason moving in.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Hannah Graham, aged 34, and his girlfriend Hannah, aged 32, wish to jointly buy a property. They have just made an offer on a house, which has been accepted. They have applied for a 90%, 25-year mortgage from Forest Bank. Whilst they are both very happy with the property, Graham is anxious to ensure the electrical system is up to modern standards, as he has powerful amplifiers for his electric guitars. He has asked if any electrical faults would be revealed in the normal mortgage process. Graham is a sales manager and has worked for his employer for two years. His basic salary is £44,000 plus commission, which was £10,000 last year but likely to be approximately £6,000 this year. Hannah started as a full-time designer for a furniture store seven years ago, but now only works part-time. Hannah receives maintenance payments of £80 per month from her ex-husband. Graham receives an income of £1,200 p.a. from a trust set up by his grandfather and will continue to do so until he reaches the age of 60. Graham and Hannah have been offered a Standard Variable Rate mortgage with a 3% discount for the first three years, but they have not yet decided upon which repayment vehicle to use. Graham favours an Equity ISA. Hannah has a more cautious attitude, and prefers a capital and interest mortgage. The Bank has valued the property in order to assess its adequacy for mortgage purposes. 2024/2025 131 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 When assessing Graham and Hannah’s borrowing capacity:
opts: details of Hannah’s previous employment are likely to be required.
the maintenance payments from Hannah’s ex-husband may be taken into account.
Hannah’s earnings will not be taken into account.
the annual income from the trust fund cannot be included.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: When considering Graham’s income for mortgage purposes, Forest Bank is likely to request:
opts: SA302s for the last three years.
details of his pension arrangements.
the extent to which commission income is guaranteed.
a detailed breakdown of the £10,000 commission earned last year.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 132 Taking into account Graham’s concern regarding the property, of what should he be advised regarding the standard mortgage process to satisfy his concerns?
opts: The valuation already carried out would have revealed all significant problems.
A full building survey would be needed to cover the level of detail he requires.
A Home Buyer’s Report would provide sufficient detail at an economic cost.
No standard survey product will be adequate for his purposes. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The 3% interest rate reduction in the second year of their proposed mortgage product:

will increase payments in year 3.
is a genuine saving which need not be repaid if the mortgage is maintained.
will be added to the capital owed.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Graham and Hannah opt for a capital and interest mortgage and the account is kept up to date, monthly payments to Forest Bank in the penultimate year of the mortgage term will:
opts: consist mainly of capital repayments.
include interest charged at a much lower rate.
comprise exclusively of interest.
be lower than payments in the previous year.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 With regard to the repayment method favoured by Hannah, of what should Graham and Hannah be made aware?
opts: The outstanding capital will not reduce during the first three years of the mortgage term.
The interest rate charged is likely to be higher than for an interest-only mortgage.
Any over payments will always be subject to an interest penalty.
There is no built-in life assurance provided.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 7 If they opt for an ISA as the repayment vehicle and Hannah subsequently becomes a non-taxpayer, what effect will this have on her eligibility to maintain her £350 share of the monthly payments?
opts: Her monthly payments must reduce to £250.
Her monthly payments must reduce to £300.
She must cease payments altogether.
She can continue her monthly payments without any restrictions.

mcqs.q: When discussing the benefits and limitations of ISAs in relation to their needs, Hannah and Graham should be advised that:
opts: a Lifetime ISA would be an ideal repayment vehicle due to the bonuses available.
it is possible to guarantee the final fund value of a stocks and shares ISA.
tax relief on the life cover to protect the mortgage is available at a rate of 20%.
they could both arrange an ISA, but could not take out a joint ISA.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 134 If Hannah and Graham proceed on an interest-only basis, with a stocks and shares ISA as their repayment vehicle, what would be the most appropriate life assurance policy for them to take, to ensure that the mortgage would be repaid in the event of either of their deaths?
opts: Convertible term assurance.
Level term assurance.
Mortgage payment protection insurance.
Mortgage protection assurance. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: When assessing how much Hannah and Graham can afford to borrow, which of the following statements is correct?
opts: Commission is not used in the affordability assessment, even if part of it is guaranteed.
Forest Bank will need to see evidence of committed expenditure only.
The affordability assessment may allow for the possibility that interest rates may increase.
The amount that Forest Bank is prepared to lend to them will be determined based solely on a multiple of their respective incomes.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Shelley has been building her self-employed mobile beauty treatment business for five years; now, aged 27, she is ready to purchase her first home. She has offered £119,000 for a leasehold flat that has been on the market for the last three months for £126,000. Her offer has now been accepted and she has asked Trevor, her adviser, to proceed with her mortgage application. The flat is in a purpose-built block of four and the vendor has advised Shelley that the upstairs neighbour is interested in buying the freehold interest. 85 years remains unexpired on the lease. With some help from her parents, Shelley has a deposit of £15,000 and requires a mortgage loan of £109,000. Trevor has recommended a Wooliwide mortgage. The rate is fixed for three years. Shelley has told Trevor that she plans to start a personal pension with St.Albans Life. Trevor has explained how this product may be used as repayment vehicle for her mortgage loan. Shelley’s business has gradually grown and her results for the past two years have been gross profits of £48,000 and net profits, which she has taken as drawings, of £40,000. Three years ago, her accounts show that she took personal drawings of £2,000 in excess of her net profits when she had the opportunity of going to Australia. 136 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies 1 In order to use a stakeholder pension to repay her mortgage, Shelley will need to accumulate a pension fund of at least:
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Shelley proceeds on the basis of linking her mortgage to the St.Albans Life pension plan, what overall rate of tax relief will she receive on the contributions to her chosen repayment vehicle?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Shelley arranges life cover for her mortgage in conjunction with her proposed mortgage repayment vehicle, what will be the most suitable product?

Whole of life assurance
Endowment assurance
Level term assurance

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If Shelley redeems her mortgage loan at the end of the fifth year, what maximum total redemption charge, if any, will apply?

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5 What maximum fee, if any, is Trevor permitted to charge Shelley in respect of the mortgage product he has recommended?

mcqs.q: Shelley maybe expected to provide three of the following in support of her mortgage application. Which one would not be required?
opts: A full set of accounts for each of the last three years.
An employer’s reference
Bank account statements.
Details of any other borrowings or substantial outgoings
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 138 What key potential advantage is obtained by opting for Shelley’s preferred mortgage repayment method compared to the opposite method of repayment?
opts: Automatic inclusion of accident and sickness cover.
A guaranteed maturity amount.
Much lower monthly payments at the outset.
Possibility of paying off the mortgage early. 2024/2025 Twelve Further Full Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What effect on Shelley’s application, is the personal drawings figure of three years ago likely to have, if any?
opts: Her application will probably be declined.
Her maximum allowable loan will be reduced.
She will be asked to provide a guarantor.
They are unlikely to have a significant impact.

mcqs.q: Under current legislation, what is Shelley’s position with regard to the purchase of the flat’s freehold?
opts: The term of the outstanding lease is too short to qualify.
There are not enough flats in the block to qualify.
At least three of the flat owners need to participate
She may apply in conjunction with the upstairs neighbour.
