mcqs.q: 2024/2025 If the fixed interest rate on Shelley’s mortgage loan is 4.99% for the first three years, what will be her monthly interest payment to the Wooliwide?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Alec and Clare have lived in a rented flat since they were married four years ago and have approached Western Bank to discuss the possibility of obtaining a mortgage. They are hoping to purchase small leasehold flat which they have seen, having successfully negotiated a £2,000 reduction in the original asking price of £112,000. The flat is one of two above a high street shop and has an unexpired lease of 75 years. Each flat and the shop comprise equal floor areas. They are both in full-time employment, earning guaranteed basic salaries of £25,000 and £22,000 respectively. Clare also receives £2,000 per annum from a lifetime trust fund. They have asked the adviser for some information on equity individual savings accounts (ISAs), as a friend has suggested that it might be a good idea to use one of these as the repayment vehicle for an interestonly mortgage. Alec is expecting a substantial salary increase when he completes his training in two years’ time, but until then, he and Clare wish to know the maximum monthly payment that they will be required to make. They also want the cheapest valuation option offered by Western Bank. The vendor has advised them that legally the freehold for this flat cannot be purchased. The bank’s affordability criteria require that mortgage payments to be no more than 80% of free disposable income. The maximum loan-to-value (LTV) is 85% without a Higher Lending Charge. As part of its affordability assessment, the bank uses figures available from the Office for National Statistics rather than exact figures. 2024/2025 141 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 Which one of the following statements is true in respect of the additional security which the bank would require if an application is approved, the property is valued at the agreed price, and Alec and Clare provide a £4,000 deposit?
opts: The provider must be encouraged to seek independent advice.
It may be possible to add the premium to the advance.
The name of the provider will be added to the mortgage deed.
The policy must be assigned to the bank.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What is the maximum that Alec and Clare could expect to borrow from Western Bank if all lending criteria are met?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: How much Stamp Duty Land Tax will be saved as a result of the lower agreed purchase price?
opts: Nil.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 142 With regard to the freehold of the flat, which factor would prohibit its purchase under current legislation?
opts: The number of flats in the block.
The floor area of each property.
The remaining term of the lease.
The purchase price of the property. 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: If Alec and Clare proceed with their preferred valuation option, what detail will this confirm?
opts: Any structural defects in the property.
The correct market price for the property.
If the electrical system meets current standards.
The amount for which the property should be insured.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which of the following mortgage products would be MOST suitable for Alec and Clare?
opts: A Bank of England base rate tracker.
A standard variable rate, currently 5.2%.
A discounted rate of 1.0% below the standard variable rate for a period of five years.
A variable rate, currently 5.2%, but capped at 5.4% for two years.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 The main benefit to Alec and Clare of the product selected in answer to the previous question is:
opts: the interest rate charged with automatically rise or fall in line with base rate.
they will know the maximum interest rate they will be charged during a given period.
they will pay less than the standard variable rate throughout a given period.
no interest penalties will be charged if they decide to make any capital reductions.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 8 With regard to the repayment vehicle in which they are interested, and the lender’s requirement for protection of the loan amount, of what should Alec and Clare be made aware?
opts: The need for a guaranteed maturity value.
Their chosen repayment vehicle automatically includes life assurance cover.
Combining their chosen repayment vehicle with decreasing term assurance will guarantee full repayment on death.
Their protection product should cover the loan amount independently of their repayment vehicle.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following would NOT be a benefit of the type of repayment vehicle being considered by Alec and Clare?
opts: The maturity date is fixed to coincide with the end of the mortgage term.
The mortgage loan may be able to be repaid early.
There is a wide choice of funds in which premiums can be invested.
The proceeds payable will not be subject to capital gains tax.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 144 What specific information do the Mortgage Conduct of Business Rules require the bank to give Alec and Clare in respect of the repayment method they are discussing with the adviser?
opts: An explanation of whether it can be continued if they move house.
A description of the types of interest rate available.
An explanation of the effect of failing to make suitable arrangements to repay the mortgage.
An illustration of the potential repayments at the end of any fixed or capped interest rate period. 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Paul and Kelly are customers of Marsh Bank, and they are seeking mortgage advice. Paul, a sole trader, works as a graphic designer. Some years ago, however, he worked for his father, who became insolvent and Paul is unsure how this might affect his proposed mortgage application. Paul’s business has been quite successful. Full sets of accounts for each of the last three years show steady profits. Last year he turned in a gross profit of £38,000. The net profit was £28,000. Kelly is an experienced systems analyst, has been employed for the last eight years and earns £24,000 p.a. gross bringing home £1,600 a month. Paul took out a 3-year car lease of £250 per month 3 months ago. The couple’s basic essential expenditure is £1,200, and their basic quality of living costs are £450 a month. They are looking to purchase a four-year-old detached house for £136,000, and have a deposit of £27,200, together with separate funds to cover legal and other costs. Marsh Bank makes a higher lending charge on loans over 75% LTV at a rate of 7.95%, The maximum loan-to-value (LTV) is 90%. Marsh Bank’s affordability criteria requires mortgage payments to be no more than 80% of free disposable income, taking into account committed expenditure, basic essential expenditure and basic quality of living costs. It used a mortgage affordability rate of 6% with works out at £6.52 per month per £1,000 borrowed. For the past five years, Paul and Kelly have had a building society mortgage of £68,000, which is interest-only and for which they have a unitised with-profits endowment policy as the repayment vehicle. They are considering a 36-month 6.75% capped rate mortgage that the bank offers, compared with its standard variable rate of 6.34%. 146 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies 1 Paul is unsure what information the bank will require in order to assess his application. Which one of the following will NOT be required?
opts: Bank reference and/or statements.
Memorandum and Articles of Association.
Profit and loss account.
Existing mortgage lender’s reference.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What effect, if any, is Paul’s father’s insolvency likely to have on any mortgage application submitted by Paul and Kelly?
opts: It should be processed on normal terms.
Only Kelly’s salary can be taken into account.
It is likely to be automatically declined.
The bank’s normal maximum criteria will be reassessed.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Assuming the purchase proceeds at the agreed price, what amount of Stamp Duty Land Tax will Paul and Kelly pay?
opts: Nil
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 What is the maximum that Paul and Kelly could expect to borrow from Marsh Bank, based on their incomes and expenditure?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5 The purpose of the higher lending charge is to protect:
opts: Paul and Kelly against long-term financial difficulty.
Paul and Kelly against a sharp fall in property prices.
the bank against any shortfall in the buildings and contents insurance.
the bank should it need to sell the property for less than the outstanding debt.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is INCORRECT with regard to the existing repayment vehicle?
opts: Policy premiums are subject to review after specified periods.
Policy premiums attract tax relief at their highest rate of income tax.
The policy will repay the existing mortgage in full on maturity, provided that all premiums have been paid when due, and the assumed growth rate has been achieved.
The proceeds on maturity will be subject to capital gains tax, but not income tax.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 148 Under the Mortgage Conduct of Business Rules, which of the following is not correct? The provider must always provide:
opts: An explanation of whether their selected mortgages terms can be continued if they move house.
A description of when their account details may be passed to credit reference agencies.

mcqs.q: Under Paul and Kelly’s preferred mortgage product, the interest rate will:
opts: not rise above the stated level for the first three years.
not change for the first three years.
only change when the standard variable rate increases.
only change if the standard variable rate changes in the first three years.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements is correct in respect of the mortgage product preferred by Paul and Kelly?
opts: Interest must be calculated on either a daily or monthly basis.
The interest rate charged will not exceed a pre-determined level during the full mortgage term.
The interest rate will always move in line with the Bank’s standard variable rate.
The interest rate will not necessarily always fall in line with the Bank’s standard variable rate.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 How much will the higher lending charge be if Paul and Kelly decide to proceed with the purchase, they borrow the maximum that the Bank will lend, and the property is valued at the agreed price?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: Greg and Cheryl have an £82,000 interest-only mortgage with the Brunswick Building Society on a property, which they own on a joint tenancy basis. A unit-linked endowment policy supports the mortgage, with a remaining term of 12 years. The plan is currently projected to have a shortfall of £17,000. Three years ago, they took out a secured personal loan for £13,500, from Kenton Finance, the proceeds of which they used to refurbish their kitchen. Repayments on the personal loan are £275 per month. Greg is employed as a full-time Administration Manager, earning £33,500 p.a., and Cheryl is a full-time physiotherapist and earns £22,500 p.a. They have two children, Michael aged 15, and Joanne aged 24. The mortgage account went into arrears for a short time three years ago, when Cheryl had to take time off work to further her studies, and they were faced with paying for Joanne’s wedding. Greg and Cheryl have now approached the society for a further advance of £27,000 to finance a loft conversion on their existing property. They intend to contribute £5,000, from their savings, towards the cost of this building work. They estimate that conversion will increase the value of their property to £135,000. The building society’s affordability criteria require mortgage payments to be no more than 75% of free disposable income. Within its calculations, it uses committed expenditure plus the ONS monthly statistical figure of £800 per couple and £150 per dependant. Brunswick used a mortgage affordability rate of 6% with works out at £6.52 per month per £1,000 borrowed. It also insists on a mortgage indemnity guarantee where the loan exceeds 80% loan to value. The maximum loan to value being 90%. Greg and Cheryl intend to use a building firm that has been recommended by some close friends. 2024/2025 151 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 1 How will the personal loan arrangement affect Greg and Cheryl’s application?
opts: The valuation of the property for mortgage purposes will be reduced by the amount of the loan outstanding.
The loan will have to be repaid as a condition of making the further advance.
The Brunswick Building Society will apply the principle of consolidation.
Payments will be taken into account as committed expenditure when assessing their ability to repay.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Greg and Cheryl’s existing repayment vehicle:
opts: does not guarantee to fully repay the loan either on death or maturity.
features tax relief on the premiums.
guarantees to fully repay the loan on either death, provided premiums are up to date.
is guaranteed to provide a tax-free surplus on maturity.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 152 Which one of the following will the Society require when processing Greg and Cheryl’s application?
opts: Evidence that planning permission has been granted.
Evidence that the design of the extension is in keeping with the neighbourhood.
Consent to the plans from Kenton Finance.
Consent of the HLC insurer. 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: The term of the further advance offered by Brunswick is most likely to be:
opts: set by mutual agreement.
the residual term of the existing policy.
the residual term of the existing mortgage.
no longer than the date of the later of Greg and Cheryl to retire.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: In relation to the further advance, tacking would be possible if:
opts: the Society postpones its prior charge.
Kenton Finance gives its agreement.
the existing life policy is made paid up.
it is consolidated with the personal loan.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Based on the building societies lending criteria, what is the MAXIMUM further advance that the society would consider assuming that the value of the property after the conversion is accurate?
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 The society is likely to impose which one of the following conditions on any further advance offer?
opts: An additional endowment policy is assigned to it.
A mortgage indemnity guarantee is arranged.
The personal loan is repaid prior to completion.
Plans and planning permission are deposited with the title deeds.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 8 In the event of Greg predeceasing Cheryl, his portion of the property will:
opts: pass as directed by his will.
be shared between Cheryl and Joanne only.
pass as a life interest to Joanne and to the children on her death.
vest automatically in Cheryl.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: When considering their endowment policy, Greg and Cheryl need to decide whether to:
opts: assign it to Kenton Finance.
extend the term of the policy.
increase the life cover.
keep it as part of their forward planning.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: D. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 154 In what way, if any, is Brunswick’s experience with Greg and Cheryl three years ago likely to affect their proposed new loan?
opts: A lien will be placed on the maximum lending.
It should not materially affect their decision.
An additional weighting will be placed on existing outgoings.
An additional guarantor will be required. 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: B. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

caseStudies.caseSummary: James and Diane purchased their flat four years ago for £130,000 with the help of an interest-only mortgage for £90,000. The repayment vehicle is a low-cost endowment policy. They are now separating and have agreed that James will pay £40,000 to Diane in return for taking full ownership of the property, which is now thought to be worth approximately £150,000. James has approached his independent adviser, Osmans plc, for advice on the possibility of seeking a further advance from his existing lender, London Bank, to fund the agreement. Diane has already vacated the property, and James has explained that he is now working in Scotland and has, therefore, let the property to a friend for a six-month period. The bank had not consented to the tenancy and indeed had actually declined James’ request to let several weeks ago. James expects to return home within 12 months, and it is likely that his new partner, Sally, will then move into the property with him. He would like her name to be added to the mortgage as soon as Diane has been released from her obligations. Sally is a regular ISA investor and has told James that she intends to use the proceeds of this ongoing investment to help repay part or the entire mortgage early. 156 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies 1 James and Diane’s impending divorce settlement:
opts: will automatically allow the lender to release Diane from her covenants.
may prevent mortgage indemnity insurance being arranged.
will not affect James’ ability to repay the loan.
will require a consent-to-mortgage form to be signed by Diane.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: Before making any firm decisions regarding the continued use of his present mortgage repayment vehicle, James’ first priority should be to:
opts: check current interim bonus rates.
ensure that it can be suitably increased.
confirm whether it is currently on target.
enquire if it remains qualifying.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What additional action is the lender likely to require to be taken in respect of the repayment vehicle?
opts: Immediate surrender, with the proceeds being applied to the mortgage account.
Transfer into James’ sole name.
Request a surrender value before making a decision.
Transfer into Diane’s sole name.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 2024/2025 What form of additional security is the lender most likely to require if the further advance is agreed?
opts: A personal guarantee.
Re-assignment of the low-cost endowment policy.
A higher lending charge.
A signed disclaimer from Diane.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: C. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: CeMAP 3 Revision Guide 5 James has been advised that if his application is successful, a new mortgage deed may not need to be drawn up because: I regulation. the loan will be exempt from II the further advance will be tacked onto the original deed. III the original mortgage deed obliges the lender to make further advances. IV there are no subsequent charges registered against the property. Which of the following is correct?
opts: I and II.
II and III.
III and IV.
I and II and III.

mcqs.q: What guidance should Osmans give James with regard to the impact of the unauthorised tenancy?
opts: His application may be refused because of the breach in the mortgage covenants.

His application is likely to be refused unless the tenant vacates the property.
The loan cannot be granted while neither borrower occupies the property.
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: 158 James has asked Osmans which additional actions may be required by London Bank. Which one of the following will NOT be required?
opts: A credit assessment check on Diane.
A property valuation.
Confirmation from a solicitor of the agreed divorce settlement.
An indication from the life assurance company on what they will allow to be done with the endowment policy. 2024/2025 Six More Full CeMAP 3 Case Studies
mcqs.ex: Correct answer: A. Derived from the revision guide answer key for this case study.

mcqs.q: What action is the lender most likely to take if it decides to formally recognise James’ friend’s status in the property?
opts: Notify the Inland Revenue.
Arrange additional buildings insurance cover.
Delay payment of the further advance, if it is agreed.

chapters.name: Clare and Nick
chapters.summary: Clare started her 25-year variable-rate interest-only mortgage ten years ago using a unit-linked endowment policy as the repayment vehicle, which is assigned to the lender. The current rate of interest currently charged is 6.4%. The loan amount was more than covered by her salary at the time, of £37,000. Since her redundancy two months ago she has been unable to find work. Clare is now two months in arrears and has no insurance policy on which to claim, although she submitted a claim for Support Mortgage Interest (SMI) as soon as she went into arrears. The ten-year review of her endowment policy shows a projected maturity value of £65,000, against the loan amount of £75,000. The insurance company has recommended an increase to her monthly premiums of £90, but Clare doesn’t want to do this and is looking for an alternative solution. Her boyfriend Nick has returned from Voluntary Service Overseas and will be moving in with her. They are planning to get married when their joint financial situation improves. In the meantime Nick will help pay the household bills and is anxious to help Clare to clear the mortgage arrears. Clare would like Nick to be added to the mortgage deed and he has agreed to this. The couple have also discussed renting their spare room to a lodger which the lender has provisionally indicated it may permit. Nick is starting a new job as a warehouse manager on an annual salary of £35,000. His employer offers no benefits package. Clare and Nick have arranged an appointment with Gerry, an adviser at their lender, to discuss their situation. Clare has had her house valued by a local estate agent who has stated that if sold, the property should be put on the market for £150,000. 2024/2025 97 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

chapters.name: Greg and Cheryl
chapters.summary: Greg and Cheryl have an £82,000 interest-only mortgage with the Brunswick Building Society on a property, which they own on a joint tenancy basis. A unit-linked endowment policy supports the mortgage, with a remaining term of 12 years. The plan is currently projected to have a shortfall of £17,000. Three years ago, they took out a secured personal loan for £13,500, from Kenton Finance, the proceeds of which they used to refurbish their kitchen. Repayments on the personal loan are £275 per month. Greg is employed as a full-time Administration Manager, earning £33,500 p.a., and Cheryl is a full-time physiotherapist and earns £22,500 p.a. They have two children, Michael aged 15, and Joanne aged 24. The mortgage account went into arrears for a short time three years ago, when Cheryl had to take time off work to further her studies, and they were faced with paying for Joanne’s wedding. Greg and Cheryl have now approached the society for a further advance of £27,000 to finance a loft conversion on their existing property. They intend to contribute £5,000, from their savings, towards the cost of this building work. They estimate that conversion will increase the value of their property to £135,000. The building society’s affordability criteria require mortgage payments to be no more than 75% of free disposable income. Within its calculations, it uses committed expenditure plus the ONS monthly statistical figure of £800 per couple and £150 per dependant. Brunswick used a mortgage affordability rate of 6% with works out at £6.52 per month per £1,000 borrowed. It also insists on a mortgage indemnity guarantee where the loan exceeds 80% loan to value. The maximum loan to value being 90%. Greg and Cheryl intend to use a building firm that has been recommended by some close friends. 2024/2025 151 CeMAP 3 Revision Guide

The bank had not consented to the tenancy and indeed had actually declined James’ request to let several weeks ago. James expects to return home within 12 months, and it is likely that his new partner, Sally, will then move into the property with him. He would like her name to be added to the mortgage as soon as Diane has been released from her obligations. chapters.name: Jayne and Liam
chapters.summary: Jayne and Liam are aged 20 and 21 respectively and are first time buyers. They are low earners despite regular overtime and long hours and are struggling to find a property they can afford. They are inquiring about shared schemes or the Right to Buy, which may help them, and Jayne’s father has offered to act as guarantor. The lender offers a scheme which would allow payments on 50% on part of the loan at 0% interest only without interest roll-up. They have seen a 100-year-old cottage which they wish to buy if they are able to obtain a loan. They know the property’s outbuildings are in serious disrepair and require extensive renovation. Liam’s Dad has just received his 25-year term Endowment Red letter from the Scottish Incredible. They are fed up and are going to sell their policy and get a repayment mortgage sorted, and the sooner, the better, as far as Liam’s Dad is concerned. Jayne and Liam have requested further information about such mortgages and their implications, but are more interested in a capital repayment mortgage, believing it to be a much cheaper option. The lender offers index-linked buildings and contents insurance, from a panel of 8 insurers but the products offered are not a condition of the mortgage. Both Jayne and Liam are employed at a Nursery in Tewkesbury. Jayne has worked there for 4 years, but Liam only joined the company 1 year ago. Each currently continues to live with their parents, but they long to be with each other. 180 2024/2025 Complete CeMAP 3 Specimen Exam

Their last 3 years’ financial records.

chapters.name: Stacey and Paul
chapters.summary: Stacey and Paul are buying their first home together in anticipation of their marriage. Their proposed property is a 70-year-old cottage, with a purchase price of £80,000, although they are prepared to pay a little more if this purchase falls through. Stacey is divorced, with a 3-year-old daughter. She has received a settlement of £20,000 from the sale of her former marital property, which will cover the deposit and expenses on the cottage. Paul is single and has been renting a flat. They are seeking a £70,000 mortgage over 25 years, on which the lender will require a Mortgage Indemnity Guarantee (HLC). Both Stacey and Paul are employed as clerical staff in a building firm; Paul earns £22,000 p.a. bringing home £1,500 a month. Stacey’s take-home pay is £930 working on a part-time basis They hope to have further children within the next 5 years when Stacey would leave work to become a full-time mother. Their employer provides a company pension scheme and full pay for sickness for up to 6 months. Both Paul and Stacey have joined the scheme. They have expressed a preference for a fixed interest rate, but are seeking advice as to which mortgage product may be most suitable. They admit to knowing very little about interest only options. They have heard about the Financial Conduct Authority and ask how it affects them. 184 2024/2025 Complete CeMAP 3 Specimen Exam

They are keen to continue this method of savings to fund their travelling and wonder if it could also be appropriate to repay their mortgage. chapters.name: Sheila and Craig
chapters.summary: 15 years ago following his separation from his wife Sheila, Craig bought a £100,000 house with a 90% mortgage. The mortgage was set up on a capital and interest basis, and monthly repayments are currently set at £480 and the capital outstanding is currently £60,000. He was also obliged to effect a mortgage indemnity guarantee policy which is underwritten by First Guarantee International (FGI). For the last three years, part of his house has been occupied by Janet, a tenant, who pays monthly rent to Craig. Two years ago, following an illness from which he has not fully recovered, he was unexpectedly made redundant. Since then he has been unsuccessful finding a new job and has exhausted all his savings. He has now built up mortgage arrears with Zebra Finance, his mortgage lender. However, following a successful interview last month Craig hopes to start a new job shortly. Meanwhile, Zebra is concerned about the level of mortgage arrears accrued and is currently in discussions with him over how this situation can be suitably addressed. During a particularly heated moment in the discussions, Zebra even threatened to apply for a possession order, backing up the threat by showing him a recent advertisement calling for last and final offers on a property Zebra have taken into possession and are about to sell. 192 2024/2025 Complete CeMAP 3 Specimen Exam
